title: Explanation and Mechanisms
text: Scientific explanation is often understood in terms of mechanisms. A mechanistic account describes entities and activities organized to produce a phenomenon. This contrasts with purely deductive-nomological pictures. Mechanistic explanation emphasizes causal organization and intervention.

title: Models as Mediators
text: Models can function as mediators between theory and world. They are not mere derivations of theory, but autonomous instruments for exploring possibilities. Idealization and approximation are central to their use. This raises questions about representation and truth.

title: Causation and Intervention
text: Interventionist accounts analyze causation in terms of hypothetical manipulations. If changing X would change Y under suitable interventions, then X is a cause of Y. This links causal claims to control and experimentation. It also suggests constraints on causal discovery methods.

title: Underdetermination and Evidence
text: The underdetermination thesis claims that evidence may be insufficient to determine a unique theory choice. Competing theories can fit the same data. Responses include appeals to theoretical virtues, background assumptions, and pragmatic constraints. The debate concerns realism and rationality.

title: Reduction and Levels
text: Reduction relates higher-level theories to lower-level accounts. Some reductions seek derivations, while others emphasize explanation across levels. Multiple realizability complicates simple reduction. Discussions often focus on biology and psychology.

title: Scientific Realism and Success
text: Realists argue that the success of science is best explained by approximate truth and reference. The no-miracles argument supports this view. Anti-realists respond with pessimistic induction and underdetermination. The dispute concerns inference to the best explanation.

title: Conceptual Change
text: Conceptual change describes how scientific concepts shift over time. Some changes are incremental, others are revolutionary. Meaning and reference can be partially preserved or radically altered. Case studies include chemistry and physics.

title: Confirmation and Bayesianism
text: Bayesian confirmation theory represents degrees of belief with probabilities. Evidence updates beliefs via conditionalization. This framework connects confirmation to likelihood and prior assumptions. Critics question whether priors can be justified objectively.
